other_people: João Paulo Coelho de Souza Rodrigues
evidence: Near-even mixture: João do Rio and the cinema/Africa titles are João Carlos Rodrigues's (about 16/31 listed citation-weight). A dança das cadeiras, A geração boêmia and Tupifilia are João Paulo Coelho de Souza Rodrigues's; Consultas jurídicas is João José Rodrigues's. Neither near-all nor clearly above the brief's two-thirds threshold; thesis overlap is unavailable.

Medicina, leis e moral (12), Hospital (4), Instituto Adolfo Lutz (3) and the health-related fragments belong to José Leopoldo Ferreira Antunes, approximately 22/40 listed citation-weight. A guerra de África, Kennedy e Salazar and the Portuguese political histories are José Freire Antunes's. Southern Exposure is Armstrong and Nelles's in a concatenated citation. Mixed, below two-thirds, with unresolved fragments and thesis overlap.

Mutual Aid, Memoirs of a Revolutionist, The Conquest of Bread and Fields, Factories and Workshops are the anarchist prince's works. The publisher identifies Peter Kropotkin as the Russian aristocrat born in 1842, deceased in 1921. Peter/Petr is a name variant; the generic Hypomnemata entry remains unassigned.

Coronelismo em Goiás (11), O Legislativo em Goiás (2), Questão agrária (2), Questões agrárias and A política tradicional are Francisco Itami Campos's, about 17/35 listed citation-weight. O Estado Nacional (9), Educação e Cultura and the Estado Novo/legal writings belong to the jurist Francisco Luís da Silva Campos. Near-even pooling; generic Goiás and damaged entries leave the exact share unresolved.

The EPHE bibliography identifies Philippe Gauthier as author of Symbola, Les cités grecques et leurs bienfaiteurs, Nouvelles inscriptions de Sardes II and Études d'histoire et d'institutions grecques. The listed Greek institutional and epigraphic studies are his; Ph. abbreviates Philippe.

Daniel Samson's Brock faculty bibliography lists The Spirit of Industry and Improvement, his editorship of Contested Countryside and 'Damn TORYISM, say I'. The accompanying rural Nova Scotia and James Barry studies belong to the same historian published as Danny Samson.

USP identifies Leila Maria Gonçalves Leite Hernandez as author of A África na sala de aula and Os filhos da terra do sol, together 28/38 listed citation-weight. The African-history articles and earlier Aliança Nacional Libertadora are hers; the LC heading abbreviates her fuller name.

História da historiografia (8), Colônia e nativismo (6), Estudos historiográficos gerais, the two Nova história em perspectiva entries and biografia da nação are Forastieri's, approximately 18/27 listed citation-weight. Modernidade em desalinho is Rogério Souza Silva's; Método e sentido is Rogério Chaves da Silva's. The display name conceals a real mixture.

The Three Worlds of Welfare Capitalism and its French translation are Gøsta Esping-Andersen's, as are the listed welfare-state studies and Welfare States in Transition chapters. The publisher also prints his name as Gosta; the missing diacritic does not identify another author.

A ferrovia do diabo (8), A evolução do sistema eleitoral brasileiro (7), O mistério do ouro dos Martírios (2) and the other twentieth-century historical/expedition works are Manoel Rodrigues Ferreira's, about 23/29 listed citation-weight. A provincia da Bahia (4) and the two 1862 Pedro I poems belong to Manoel Jesuíno Ferreira.
